messages:
pagerduty: INCIDENT 1901 triggered -> service: inference-gateway, symptom: queues growing, error: scale-up failing, priority: P1

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded 1901234500 -> release/production@v3.4.2 rolling, 12 pods scheduled

Maria (oncall): seeing huge request queue in us-east1, latency > 8s p95 and token drop warnings. Autoscaler shows pending pods in Pending state for > 6m.

Chris (SRE): checking k8s events, multiple pods Pending due to 'Insufficient nvidia-gpu' in nodepool-gpu-us-east1. Looks like region quota/limit hit on GCP.

Anita (Infra): confirmed with cloud metrics — GPU quota usage in us-east1 at 100% of quota, preemptible and standard pools exhausted. No additional GPU machines can be created.

Maria (oncall): customer impact: some hosted customers on dedicated routing see 429s and degraded throughput; non-critical background jobs queued. Notifying CS.

Ben (Prod Eng): is the autoscaler mis-configured to request new node types? any chance we're asking for custom accelerator types?

Anita (Infra): autoscaler is requesting standard T4-equivalent instance groups. Quota is at project-level per-region. Also we have some ephemeral jobs (training) in project causing fragmentation.

Chris (SRE): immediate mitigation plan: 1) divert non-prod and low-priority traffic to fallback model/CPU; 2) route high-tier customers to dedicated capacity in us-west2; 3) open cloud support quota increase.

Maria (oncall): doing (1) now — switching low-priority route to compact-quant model. command: 
```
# update route to fallback model
curl -X POST "$REDWOOD_API/routes/low-prio/update" -d '{"model":"compact-q4", "priority":"low"}'
```

deploy-bot: route update applied to 3 services in 27s.

Sam (Sales Eng): pinging top-affected customer accounts (acct-45, acct-99) to set expectations. They reported elevated errors 5m ago.

Anita (Infra): opened GCP support case #CASE-78321 requesting quota bump for GPUs in us-east1. ETA uncertain. Also requesting that org quota be consolidated to free unused training accounts.

Ben (Prod Eng): Can we temporarily spin up smaller clusters in us-west2 and failover traffic? What about cross-region latency?

Chris (SRE): we can failover critical routes to us-west2. Latency will increase ~30-70ms depending on customer origin, but preferable to 429s. I'll flip the routing policy for tagged critical flows.

Maria (oncall): flipping routing policy for tag:critical -> us-west2 now. command: 
```
# set routing policy
redwood route set --from-tag critical --to-region us-west2 --weight 100
```

Maria (oncall): policy applied. Early checks: critical queue length dropping in us-east1 by ~40% as traffic is diverted. P95 latency for critical down to 200ms (good).

Anita (Infra): provisioning dedicated reserved capacity pool in us-west2 for emergency is in progress; requesting uplift on billing/commit. Preemptible pools were already maxed; provisioning non-preemptible nodes will take ~7-12m.

Chris (SRE): temporary token-throttling enabled for non-critical customers to shed 30% traffic. config: "rate_limit: non_critical: 70pct"

Ben (Prod Eng): I see some backlog items that can be worker-processed later. Kicking off background requeue to slow consumers.

Ops (bot): NOTE: 3 alerts suppressed during mitigation window per SRE policy.

Maria (oncall): updating incident channel and creating incident summary for CS. Customers impacted: some hosted API users, background batch jobs delayed; enterprise Dedicated customers routed successfully to their pinned capacity.

Sam (Sales Eng): filed proactive notices to customers via status.redwood.ai and direct emails to affected enterprise contacts.

Anita (Infra): cloud support replied — initial response: case acknowledged, engineer assigned, estimated review 2-6 hours. They recommended temporary quota project reallocation, but that requires org owners.

Chris (SRE): secondary mitigation — enable model quantization fallback on the gateway for 20% of requests to reduce GPU need. Rolling config change in 3,2,1...

deploy-bot: config rollout completed across 5 clusters.

Maria (oncall): queue growth stabilized, pending pods count down to 0 in us-east1, warnings clearing. Still monitoring for any regressions.

Chris (SRE): next steps: follow up on GCP case for permanent quota bump or cross-project allocation; cleanup training accounts hogging GPUs; formal postmortem to cover autoscaler heuristics and routing policy to avoid single-region saturation.

Maria (oncall): handing off to Chris for long-running follow-ups. I'll put a summary in ops-runbooks and tag for postmortem. Handoff at 03:40 UTC.

Chris (SRE): taking over. If anything spikes, page me @here. Creating postmortem issue now: GH-4121.

Sam (Sales Eng): thanks team — customers updated and support tickets linked.

Anita (Infra): note for postmortem: consider implementing regional soft-fairshare to block long-running training from starving inference pools.

Maria (oncall): incident resolved for now; marking P1 -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:

pagerduty: Incident 1901 acknowledged by Maria (oncall) and transferred to Chris (SRE).

Chris (SRE): closing thread, leaving follow-ups in GH-4121 and infra runbook updates.
